data.text:
Tropical depression nineteen, named Isang in the Philippines late Friday evening, has since organized and intensified into a tropical storm, warning the international name of Kajiki. 
From here forth, we will refer to the storm by its international name. 
Kajiki still remains a broad system, but has organized at an alarming speed in the past few hours. 
7 hours ago, the storm packed winds of 46km/h, with gusts of 65. 
Now Kajiki boasts sustained winds of 74km/h with gusts of 93km/h. 

Kajiki is forecasted to  intensify over the next 24 hours, but intensity spread in model projections is quite wide based on a few factors. 
Kajiki still holds a considerably broad core, though significant consolidation rates are ongoing, which should shrink the core and aid in intensification as it approaches Hainan. 

The storm is forecasted to upgrade into a T5 storm (167 to 212km/h) within 24 hours according to the ECMWF. 
GFS is more modest, with the system possibly reaching low-end T4 intensity (120 to 130km/h) 

ICON expects the systems core to remain broad until consolidation in the Gulf of Tonkin Sunday night, and thus, the system is projected weaker, as a T3 storm with winds of 90 to 110km/h expected in Kajiki in 24 hours. 

That said, our forecast is then coming out to be sustained winds of 120 to 150km/h by midday Sunday. 

Another tricky one is the landfall itself in Hainan Sunday afternoon, forecasted to occur over far southern Hainan as a compact storm by the GFS and ECMWF, but ICON projects a direct landfall effecting essentially the entire province due to the broader structure of the storm projection. 

In GFS and ECMWF’s scenario, southern Hainan may be battered with typhoon level winds of 120 to 140km/h near Sanya. 
but ICON is less intense but more widespread, with 70 to 100km/h gusts expected over all coasts of the province. 
Rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches can be expected, with much higher and more dangerous amounts of 7 to 9 inches possible over coastal sections. 
At this time, southern Hainan should prepare for destructive winds Sunday afternoon and evening, and the rest of Hainan should be on be aware strong winds are possible in this timeframe. 
Life-threatening flash flooding is expected over southern sections. 

From there, Kajiki will track west over the Gulf of Tonkin, and models are in agreement for rapid intensification. 
ECMWF remains the most intense, and 60 hours from now, Monday evening, the model anticipates T6 intensity with near 220km/h winds. 
GFS is only somewhat more modest, at T5 intensity with winds of 185km/h, and similar numbers on the ICON. 

Landfall in Vietnam is forecasted to be much more severe then over Hainan, with Kajiki making landfall at peak intensity, with sustained winds anywhere from 170 to 210km/h expected. 

Powerful winds, with gusts between 140 to 180km/h is currently expected over the direct impact zone, but where the precise landfall will occur also is difficult to determine at this time. 
Rainfall is also forecast to be extreme, with uncertainty prevailing as well, and rainfall totals widely ranging between 10 to 20 inches from Dong Ha to Thanh Hoa are currently expected. 

ICON has the storm making landfall near Thanh Hoa, but ECMWF, GFS, and ACCESS are all in agreement for a landfall further south, near Ba Don. 
We are also currently expecting the storm to make landfall near Ba Don. 
Kajiki is a priority storm based on it’s potential, and frequent updates will follow. The next will be posted at 5:00 am Sunday, stay tuned!
